extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system; researchers and students in computational/commutative algebra who use SINGULAR library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (grwalk.lib, homolog.lib, etc.): usage signatures, preconditions, return values, and worked examples for each procedure. Intended to guide users invoking these library procedures and understanding their outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: lsum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lsum(L); L list. Assume: L is a list of things with the binary operator + defined. Return: The sum of the elements of L. Theory: Sums the elements of a list. (Note: Eventually this will be deleted and become a more efficient kernel function.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: LIB "ellipticcovers.lib"; list L = 1,2,3,4,5; lsum(L); → 15. Use when you have a list whose elements support +; this is a simple convenience routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: grwalk lib (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: grwalk.lib. Purpose: Groebner Walk Conversion Algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Header documenting that procedures in this library implement Groebner-walk-style conversion algorithms; see cross-references to rwalk.lib and swalk.lib for related algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: fwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: fwalk(ideal i); fwalk(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal w.r.t. the lexicographical ordering or a weighted-lex ordering, calculated via the fractal walk algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided with LIB "grwalk.lib"; ring and ideal setup; fwalk(I) returns a list of polynomials forming the standard basis. See cross-references: awalk1, awalk2, gwalk, pwalk, twalk, std/stdfglm for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: twalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: twalk(ideal i); twalk(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal w.r.t. the ordering "(a(w),lp)" or "(a(1,0,...,0),lp)", calculated via the Tran algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows usage with ring and ideal; returns standard basis. Cross-references to other walk algorithms and standard basis commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: awalk1
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: awalk1(ideal i); awalk1(ideal i, int n); awalk1(ideal i, int n, intvec v, intvec w); awalk1(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal, calculated via the first alternative algorithm from an ordering "(a(v),lp)", "dp" or "Dp" to the ordering "(a(w),lp)" or "(a(1,0,...,0),lp)" with a perturbation degree n for the weight vector w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show invocation and returned basis. Cross-references: awalk2, fwalk, gwalk, pwalk, twalk, and standard basis commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: awalk2
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: awalk2(ideal i); awalk2(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal, calculated via the second alternative algorithm from the ordering "(a(v),lp)", "dp" or "Dp" to the ordering "(a(w),lp)" or "(a(1,0,...,0),lp)".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage provided; returns standard basis. Cross-references to other related walk procedures and std/stdfglm.

rubrics_metrics.name: pwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: pwalk(int d, ideal i, int n1, int n2); pwalk(int d, ideal i, int n1, int n2, intvec v, intvec w); Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal, calculated via the perturbation walk algorithm from the ordering "(a(v),lp)", "dp" or "Dp" to the ordering "(a(w),lp)" or "(a(1,0,...,0),lp)" with a perturbation degree n, m for v and w, resp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: pwalk(I,2,2); returns standard basis. Use when a perturbation-degree-controlled walk is desired; see related walk procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: gwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: gwalk(ideal i); gwalk(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal, calculated via the improved Groebner walk algorithm from the ordering "(a(v),lp)", "dp" or "Dp" to the ordering "(a(w),lp)" or "(a(1,0,...,0),lp)".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing a Groebner basis wrt lp for a complicated ideal; returns a list of basis elements. Cross-references to awalk1/2, fwalk, pwalk, twalk and to std/stdfglm.

rubrics_metrics.name: canonMap
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: canonMap(id); id = ideal/module. Return: a list L giving the kernel in two different representations and the cokernel of the canonical map M → Ext^c_R(Ext^c_R(M,R),R) given by presentations. Here M is the R-module (R=basering) given by the presentation defined by id, i.e. M=R/id resp. M=R^n/id; c is the codimension of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output structure: L[1] is the preimage of the kernel in R resp. R^n; L[2] is a presentation of the kernel; L[3] is a presentation of the cokernel. Examples show calls with ideals and modules and the printed components. Use when analyzing canonical double-Ext maps and their kernels/cokernels.

rubrics_metrics.name: cup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cup(M[, any, any]); M = module. Compute: cup-product Ext^1(M',M') × Ext^1(M',M') → Ext^2(M',M'), where M' := R^m/M if M in R^m, R basering (i.e. M' := coker(matrix(M))). If called with >=2 arguments: compute symmetrized cup-product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume all Ext's are finite dimensional. Returns: with 1 arg → matrix whose columns present coordinates of b_i & b_j wrt a k-basis of Ext^2; with 2 args → symmetric (1/2)(b_i&b_j + b_j&b_i); with 3 args → list L where L[1] is matrix (symmetric case), L[2] k-basis matrix of Ext^1, L[3] k-basis matrix of Ext^2. printlevel controls verbosity (>=1 shows progress, >=2 shows alternative representations, >=3 shows detailed lifting information). Note: to compute cup-product of M itself, apply proc to syz(M). Several worked examples illustrate returned matrices and interpretation as bilinear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: cupproduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cupproduct(M,N,P,p,q[,any]); M,N,P modules, p,q integers. Compute: cup-product Ext^p(M',N') × Ext^q(N',P') → Ext^(p+q)(M',P'), where M' := R^m/M if M in R^m (i.e. M' := coker(matrix(M))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume all Ext's are finite dimensional. If called with 5 args returns matrix whose columns present coordinates of products (b_i & c_j) wrt a k-basis of Ext^(p+q); with 6 args returns list L: L[1] = matrix, L[2] = k-basis matrix of Ext^p(M',N'), L[3] = k-basis matrix of Ext^q(N',P'), L[4] = k-basis matrix of Ext^(p+q)(N',P'). printlevel >=1 shows progress; >=2 shows results in another representation. For computing cupproduct of M,N themselves, apply to syz(M), syz(N). Extensive examples demonstrate k-bases, liftings, and how to read the final matrices as bilinear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: depth(M[, I]); M module, I ideal. Return: int. If called with 1 argument: the depth of M' = coker(M) wrt basering (assumed local). If called with 2 arguments: the depth of M' = coker(M) wrt the ideal I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure uses KoszulHomology. Examples show depth of specified modules/ideals in both affine and local rings; illustrates behavior with various choices of I (e.g., maxideal, principal ideals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext_R
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Ext_R(v, M[, p]); v int resp. intvec, M module, p int. Compute: a presentation of Ext^k(M', R) for k = v[1], v[2], ... where M' = coker(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a free resolution 0 ← M' ← F0 ← F1 ← F2 ← ... and its dual sequence, Ext^k = ker(A_{k+1})/im(A_k) is presented. Return: if v is int → module Ext; if v is intvec → list of Ext^k; with third int arg returns list l with l[1]=module Ext^k, l[2]=SB (standard basis) of Ext^k, l[3]=matrix representing k-basis of Ext^k (if finite dimensional). printlevel controls verbosity: >=0 prints affine dimension; >=1 prints Ak, Ak+1 and k-basis of Ext^k in Fk*. Default uses mres; can pass "sres" to use sres. If input module had attribute isHomog it is propagated to output. Examples illustrate computing Ext^i over quotient rings and interpreting returned k-bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Ext(v, M, N[, any]); v int resp. intvec, M,N modules. Compute: a presentation of Ext^k(M', N') for k = v[1], v[2], ... where M' = coker(M) and N' = coker(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm constructs appropriate Hom complexes and computes K = modulo(A_{k+1}, B), J = module(A_k) + module(C), and Ext = modulo(K, J), yielding a presentation of Ext^k(M',N'). Return semantics mirror Ext_R: module Ext if v int, list if intvec, and if additional arg present returns list with module, SB, and k-basis matrices. printlevel >=0 prints dimensions; >=1 prints Ak, Ak+1 and k-bases in Hom(Fk,G0). Examples demonstrate computing Ext^k over rings and reading intermediate matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fitting(M, n); M module, n int. Return: ideal, (standard basis of) n-th Fitting ideal of M' = coker(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: computing various fitting(M,k) for a given presentation matrix; outputs lists of generators for the Fitting ideal for different indices, including special cases (fitting(M,2) → 1). Useful for determining minors and determinantal conditions describing module support.

rubrics_metrics.name: flatteningStrat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: flatteningStrat(M); M module. Return: list of ideals. The list entries L[1],...,L[r] describe the flattening stratification of M' = coker(M): setting L[0] = 0, L[r+1] = 1, the flattening stratification is given by the open sets Spec(A/V(L[i-1])) \ V(L[i]), i=1,...,r+1 (A = basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes refer to the textbook 'A Singular Introduction to Commutative Algebra' for more information. Example given showing how the output lists are the defining ideals for strata; useful for geometric analysis of module-flatness behavior over parameter spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Hom(M, N[, any]); M, N = modules. Compute: a presentation of Hom(M', N'), M' = coker(M), N' = coker(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: from presentations F1 → F0 → M' and G1 → G0 → N', build exact sequences relating Hom(F*,G*) and compute D = modulo(A, B), Hom = modulo(D, C). Return: module Hom; with 3rd arg returns list l with l[1]=Hom, l[2]=SB of Hom, l[3]=k-basis of coker(Hom) (if finite dimensional) represented as elements in Hom(F0, G0). printlevel controls output detail: >=0 prints affine dimension, >=1 prints D and C and k-basis in Hom(F0,G0), >=2 prints basis elements as matrices F0→G0. Multiple examples illustrate reading columns of output as basis elements and the meaning of D and C.

rubrics_metrics.name: homology
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homology(A, B, M, N); Let M and N be submodules of R^m and R^n presenting M' = R^m/M, N' = R^n/N (R = basering) and let A,B matrices inducing maps R^k --A--> R^m --B--> R^n. Compute a presentation of ker(B)/im(A). If B induces a map M' → N' (i.e. B*M = 0) and im(A) ⊆ ker(B) (i.e. B*A = 0) then ker(B)/im(A) is the homology of the complex R^k --A--> M' --B--> N'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: module H, a presentation of ker(B)/im(A). Note: homology returns a free module of rank m if ker(B) = im(A). Examples show computing homology in quotient rings and returning generators and vdim/dim of the homology module.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isCM(M); M module. Return: 1 if M' = coker(M) is Cohen–Macaulay; 0 otherwise. Assume: basering is local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: isCM applied to modules in a local polynomial ring returns 0/1 accordingly. Use to test Cohen–Macaulay property of module quotients in local contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: isFlat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isFlat(M); M module. Return: 1 if M' = coker(M) is flat; 0 if this is not the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example beginnings shown (truncated in this chunk). Use to test flatness of module presentations; typical usage within deformation/parameter space contexts.
